guides.title: Installation and portable use
guides.summary: Install a packaged build or run the portable directory in place.

steps.text: Use the browser editor without installing, or download a desktop release.
Extract the archive or run the platform installer.
Keep bin/shaders, bin/fonts, and bin/assets beside the executables.
Launch arcflow_editor; no global dependency installation is required.
Use arcflow_compiler --version to verify channel and format versions.
Projects and user settings live outside the application install tree.

guides.title: Your first animation
guides.summary: Draw a shape, add two keys, and make it move.

steps.text: Draw a rectangle with R.
steps.detail: Click and drag on the canvas. Start a blank project from File > New From Template if you want an empty workspace. The walkthrough also works with your current project.

steps.text: Select the shape with Pick (V).
steps.detail: V toggles Pick and Node. Choose Pick, then click the shape or its name in Layers. Drag the shape to its starting position.

steps.text: At time zero, choose POSITION and add the first key.
steps.detail: Use the property chooser above the timeline, then click + First key or press K. Create this key before moving to a later time.

steps.text: Move the playhead to one second and move the shape.
steps.detail: Once a Position track exists, dragging the shape creates or updates the key at the current time. Two diamonds on the track define the motion.

steps.text: Press Space to play, then pause.
steps.detail: Press F6 for Curves. Select the Position track, apply Ease both, and press F to fit the graph. You can undo any change with Ctrl+Z.

steps.text: Save the editable project with Ctrl+S.
steps.detail: Keep the .afproj file for later edits. In a browser this downloads the file; store that download somewhere you can find it. Use File > Export when you are ready to share.

guides.title: Animate vector points and Bezier handles
guides.summary: Every editable path point and cubic handle can have its own track.

steps.text: Create a Path or open the Vector Animation example.
Use Node (V) to select a point; choose PATH POINT, HANDLE IN, or HANDLE OUT in the timeline.
Move the playhead and press K before and after changing the selected handle.
Use Curve Editor to tune interpolation without changing path topology.
Preview with Space; point and handle tracks evaluate together.
Remove point tracks before adding or deleting path commands.

guides.title: Interactive button workflow
guides.summary: Build visual button states and exercise pointer or keyboard activation.

steps.text: Open the Interactive Button example and select the button background.
Edit the background, focus ring, and icon directly in Layers.
Use the Press Feedback clip to animate scale, color, and opacity.
Compile and send pointer down/up or keyboard activate through the C API.
Poll runtime events and let the host perform application actions.
Authoring state-machine bindings are limited; host event wiring is required.

guides.title: Responsive UI and safe areas
guides.summary: Anchors, percent sizing, layout direction, and safe areas adapt a canvas.

steps.text: Open the Responsive UI example and select a layout-managed object.
Use Inspector layout controls to cycle fixed, percent, and intrinsic sizing.
Set anchors and pivots before adjusting offsets and minimum sizes.
Configure the root safe area and Fit, Fill, or Stretch canvas scaling.
Resize the window and inspect ruler measurements at multiple aspect ratios.

guides.title: Particle effect authoring
guides.summary: Emitters expose spawning, forces, output, collisions, LOD, and trails.

steps.text: Open the Particle Effect example and select the Emitter object.
Use the Inspector pages to set spawn shape, lifetime, velocity, and color.
Tune force, collision, trail, flipbook, and output pages as needed.
Preview at several zoom levels; particles remain canvas-clipped.
Set capacity and LOD before compiling to bound runtime cost.

guides.title: Embed the Arcflow C runtime
guides.summary: Load a compiled package, create an instance, update it, and release handles.

steps.text: Include arcflow/arcflow_runtime.h and link arcflow_runtime.
Fill AfRuntimeCreateInfo; frames_in_flight must be one or two.
Call af_runtime_create, af_package_load, then af_instance_create.
Call play/update, resize, input, property, and event functions from the host.
Destroy instance before package, then destroy the runtime.
See the shipped runtime_sample.c; it is built and tested with every release.

guides.title: Vulkan host integration
guides.summary: Arcflow accepts an existing Vulkan device and graphics queue.

steps.text: Create a Vulkan 1.3 instance, physical device, logical device, and queue.
Pass all four Vulkan handles plus the graphics queue family together.
Keep those handles alive until every Arcflow runtime instance is destroyed.
Use host-owned command buffers only through the versioned host SDK contract.
Arcflow does not own presentation, queue submission, waits, or device teardown.
Check runtime and package ABI versions before loading external content.

guides.title: Project and package formats
guides.summary: .afproj is deterministic authoring text; .afp is validated runtime data.

steps.text: Commit .afproj text and project-relative asset sources to source control.
Never hand-edit .afp packages; regenerate them with arcflow_compiler.
Resolve <<<<<<<, =======, and >>>>>>> markers before opening a project.
Use --validate-project, --check-determinism, and --validate in CI.
Unknown future format versions are rejected before allocation or execution.

guides.title: C API reference map
guides.summary: The installed public headers are the authoritative declarations.

steps.text: Runtime lifetime: af_runtime_create and af_runtime_destroy.
Packages: af_package_load and af_package_destroy.
Instances: create, destroy, update, play, pause, stop, seek, and resize.
Input: pointer, keyboard, controller, state inputs, triggers, and events.
Bindings: property_id, property type, get, set, format, and locale.
Accessibility and VFX controls are declared in arcflow_runtime.h.

guides.title: Troubleshooting
guides.summary: Use validation first, then isolate project, package, platform, or GPU state.

steps.text: Run --validate-project; repair missing assets and merge markers first.
Run --check-determinism and compile a release package again.
Open Workspace > System / Displays for DPI, input, and Vulkan capabilities.
Use F11 project validation and F10 profiler inside the editor.
Keep generated captures when reporting visual or driver-specific problems.
Unsupported GPU capabilities fail explicitly instead of silently degrading.

guides.title: Performance workflow
guides.summary: Measure frame time, then reduce the subsystem shown to be expensive.

steps.text: Use F10 to inspect frame time, scene size, animation keys, and allocations.
Bound particle capacity and use LOD before reducing visual quality globally.
Pack atlases and avoid unnecessary image dimensions and duplicated assets.
Keep vector topology stable and use the fewest useful animated points.
Use release packages for representative measurements.

guides.title: Security boundaries
guides.summary: Treat projects, packages, plugins, and update artifacts as untrusted input.

steps.text: Validate sizes, formats, runtime ABI, and package versions before use.
Use atomic writes and rotating backups for project and staged update files.
Require signature verification before accepting an update artifact.
Only register trusted editor plugins and validate compiler-transform output.
Do not expose arbitrary host files through runtime or plugin callbacks.

guides.title: Project and runtime migration
guides.summary: Migrate authoring data forward while keeping the original recoverable.

steps.text: Keep the original project and its asset directory under source control.
Open the project in the new editor and review migration diagnostics.
Save to a new path first when crossing more than one format generation.
Validate and compile again; do not reuse packages from an incompatible ABI.
Downgrade by restoring source control, not by editing version fields.

guides.title: Keyboard shortcut reference
guides.summary: F1 opens the live, configurable shortcut list for the current build.

steps.text: Ctrl+N/O/S create, open, and save; Ctrl+Shift+S saves as.
F5 compiles, Space previews, K adds a key, F6 opens Curves, and Shift+F6 opens Frames.
Ctrl+Z/Y undo and redo; Ctrl+C/V/D copy, paste, and duplicate.
Ctrl+F searches hierarchy; Ctrl+Shift+P opens the command palette.
Use the toolbar for grid and snapping; Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen.
Open Help > Keyboard Shortcuts to inspect or rebind every command.

guides.title: Known limitations
guides.summary: Current constraints are explicit so projects can plan around them.

steps.text: Desktop targets are Linux x64 and Windows x64; the browser build also runs the editor and player.
Cloud collaboration is not built in; use standard source control and locks.
Lottie import remains unavailable. Lottie JSON and dotLottie export cover core vector motion; advanced SVG/VFX features may require GIF, MP4, or .afp.
Interactive state-machine authoring is less complete than runtime playback.
Automatic updates are opt-in and require a host-provided signature verifier.
Desktop rendering uses Vulkan; the browser uses Canvas 2D. Export and platform capabilities differ.

guides.title: Frame-by-frame drawing
guides.summary: Create independent vector drawings and turn them into a flipbook.

steps.text: Open Frames with Shift+F6.
steps.detail: You can also click Frames beside the timeline timecode. Frame 1 is time zero. Existing ordinary objects remain visible as backgrounds.

steps.text: Draw on the current frame.
steps.detail: Use the existing shape, pen, or freehand tools. Drawing in an empty cell creates a drawing group automatically. Each group holds that frame’s editable objects.

steps.text: Click Duplicate and change the new drawing.
steps.detail: The copy is independent. Duplicate and + Blank move to the next empty cell, skipping occupied and held cells. Use + Blank when you want to redraw from scratch.

steps.text: Step with [ and ] and turn on Onion skin.
steps.detail: The previous drawing appears blue and the next appears pink. Ghosts are references: they cannot be selected through the active frame, and they do not appear in exports.

steps.text: Use Hold + to extend a drawing into empty cells.
steps.detail: A held drawing stays visible for several frames. Hold cannot overwrite the next drawing. Every cell in the hold edits the same drawing.

steps.text: Set FPS and click Fit clip length.
steps.detail: FPS changes the speed of drawing exposures. Fit clip length trims trailing empty time while retaining ordinary animation keys. Enlarge the timeline if this button is hidden.

steps.text: Preview with Space and save with Ctrl+S.
steps.detail: Pause before editing. Undo restores drawings and their timing. .afproj preserves all frames; .afp and Lottie export keep their stepped visibility. GIF/MP4 export requires FFmpeg.

guides.title: Shape motion in the graph
guides.summary: Use easing presets and handles to control the feel of a movement.

steps.text: Create two keys for a property.
steps.detail: Follow Your first animation if you do not have a track yet. Select its row in the timeline; the graph displays the selected object and property.

steps.text: Press F6 for Curves, then F to fit.
steps.detail: The horizontal axis is time. The vertical axis shows actual property values. Use X/Y or RGBA to inspect one component of a multi-value property.

steps.text: Select a key and choose an easing preset.
steps.detail: Linear has constant interpolation. Hold keeps the previous value. Ease in, Ease out, Ease both, and Overshoot shape the segment after the selected key.

steps.text: Drag a handle to adjust the transition.
steps.detail: The handles belong to the segment after the selected key. Constant segments and final keys have no handles. Overshoot can move beyond the endpoint values.

steps.text: Drag keys horizontally to retime.
steps.detail: Box-select several keys, or use Shift/Ctrl-click to change selection. Wheel zooms; Shift+wheel pans. Escape cancels an active drag.

steps.text: Play the motion and save.
steps.detail: When the timeline has focus, Delete, duplicate, copy, and paste work on keys. Click the canvas before using those commands on objects. Ctrl+Z restores an edit.

guides.title: Draw and animate gradients
guides.summary: Apply a gradient to a fill or outline, then animate it.

steps.text: Draw or select a shape.
steps.detail: Choose Fill or Outline in the Inspector. An outline needs a visible stroke width; use the same value controls to type, drag, or step the width.

steps.text: Press Shift+G and choose a gradient type.
steps.detail: Choose Linear, Radial, or Conic. Drag across the selected object to set the gradient. You can move its handles directly on the canvas.

steps.text: Adjust the stops and their colors.
steps.detail: Select a stop to change its position or color. RGB, alpha, and hex fields accept typing, dragging, and minus/plus steps. Hex stepping changes the RGB number.

steps.text: Choose a gradient property in the timeline.
steps.detail: For example, choose GRAD START, GRAD END, GRAD ANGLE, or STOP COLOR. Keep the relevant Fill/Outline target and stop selected. Add a key at the starting time.

steps.text: Move to a later time and adjust the gradient.
steps.detail: After the track exists, edits update the current key. Add another key if needed, then preview. Keep the same stop structure while animating its values.

steps.text: Save the project and check your export.
steps.detail: The editable project retains fill and outline gradients. Export support varies by format: preview the result and use rendered output or .afp if a vector format cannot represent an effect.

guides.title: Save, reopen, and share
guides.summary: Keep an editable original and choose the right format for delivery.

steps.text: Save the source project with Ctrl+S.
steps.detail: Use .afproj for continued editing. In a browser, a normal download is created and a download-ready link appears. Keep the downloaded file; browser storage is not your only backup.

steps.text: Open a project with Ctrl+O.
steps.detail: Choose an .afproj file using the file picker. Opening another project can ask you to save or discard unsaved changes. Image assets must remain available or be embedded.

steps.text: Open File > Export.
steps.detail: Choose .afp for Arcflow playback, SVG for a static vector image, or Lottie for supported vector animation. Test the resulting file in its intended viewer.

steps.text: For drawing frames, fit the clip before exporting.
steps.detail: Frames > Fit clip length keeps the useful animation range. Preview it first to check holds, timing, and any background objects.

steps.text: Use GIF or MP4 for a rendered animation.
steps.detail: These exports need FFmpeg in the desktop environment. Browser builds cannot run the desktop FFmpeg process; use a supported vector/runtime export or open the project on desktop.

steps.text: Reopen the saved source once before archiving.
steps.detail: Store the .afproj, any external asset files, and exported delivery files together. When sharing a bug, include a small reproducible project and the editor build version.
